summary: Extensions should couple compute disclosure to requested work, signed provenance, external validation, and efficiency rather than celebrate the largest number.

items.text: Create maintainer-approved compute grants for a specific issue, benchmark, or release question, with a budget ceiling, expected artifacts, expiry, and named reviewer.
Sign the contribution statement and bind it to the source revision, workflow, generated artifacts, and validation results; archive the acceptance rationale with the project decision history.
Report an efficiency-normalized effort fingerprint beside raw compute so maintainers can compare equivalent task classes without treating larger spend as better.
Require sponsored outputs to pass the same public tests and policy checks as all other contributions, and publish failed validation rather than only successful runs.
